findings.where: First screen, top navigation: 'Profile', 'Articles and talks' and 'Blog' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: All three nav items go to the same place, the article specimen (#article). 'Profile' opens a blog post on PPP law instead of anything about Mark, and the three items can't be told apart by where they lead.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer checking Mark's background clicks 'Profile' to see who he is and lands mid-page in an article. They get the wrong idea of what the nav offers, and the founder, who judges this first screen 'exactly as a visitor sees it', sees a nav that doesn't work.

findings.where: Article specimen, the download row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · PDF'
findings.fault: The row is labelled PDF and marked with a download arrow, but the link goes to #article, the top of the same article. No PDF opens or downloads, so the action the row promises is dead.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants the lecture slides clicks 'PDF' and the page jumps back up to the article's heading. The research names the PDF list as 'the product', so this is the one deep action the specimen exists to show.

findings.where: Article specimen, the numbers on the three-item list (1., 2., 3.)
findings.fault: The list numbers are set in house blue, the page's link colour, but they can't be clicked. That breaks the specimen's own stated rule, 'blue only where something can be clicked'.
findings.who_objects: A reader who has learned that blue means a link meets blue numbers that do nothing. Every list Angélique adds will repeat this beside prose that will hold real blue links, so the link colour stops meaning only 'link'.

findings.fault: It's a button (it does something on the page), but it looks exactly like a navigation link: blue, underlined text with no button edge or fill. Nothing tells the visitor it replays an animation here rather than taking them somewhere.
findings.who_objects: The founder testing the motion sketch expects the click to go somewhere, as the underline suggests, rather than an in-place replay. The underline is reserved for links, so the look means two functions.

findings.where: First screen header, 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark
findings.fault: The name and the mark read as one lockup in the place a home link usually sits, but only the mark is a link. The name, which the brief puts first, does nothing when clicked.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on any inner page who clicks the name, the larger and first element of the lockup, to get home finds it doesn't work, while the smaller mark beside it does.
